The issue is clear: the "Actions" group (which contains the theme "Switch Mode" toggle) is hidden whenever you're in search mode (`!isSearchMode && ...` on line 185), so typing anything filters it out entirely. Let me make the action commands participate in local search instead.

Looking at the search functionality, I see the issue: when search mode is active (searchValue.length >= 2), the Actions group gets hidden because of the condition checking `!isSearchMode`, but the Jump to commands still display regardless of whether they match the search term. The user wants the switch mode to be included in the search results and filtered accordingly.

I'll add a helper function to match command labels against the search value, then modify the actions to be filtered and shown even during search mode when they match the query text.

content.text: Now update the render condition so actions show in search mode when they match.

I'm reconsidering whether Jump to items should be filtered like the other search results, but they're existing behavior that always displays with the quoted search, so I'll leave them as is. Let me check the lints now.

Done. The theme toggle now shows up in search.

What I changed in `command-menu.tsx`:
- Added a `matchesSearch` helper that does a case-insensitive substring match on a command's label.
- `visibleActions` now includes an action while searching when its label matches the query (e.g. typing "mode", "dark", "light", or "switch" surfaces the "Switch Dark/Light Mode" item). When not searching, all actions show as before.
- The "Actions" group renders whenever there are matching actions (removed the `!isSearchMode` guard).
- `showNoResults` now also accounts for matching actions, so "No results found" doesn't appear when an action still matches.

Your message trailed off at "make the " — if there was something else you wanted (e.g. also make the "Jump to" items filter by the query, or add more searchable actions), let me know and I'll fold it in.
